items.title: Section: The Tenth and Final Ground Opens — Ready to Become Dharma-King, Recalling the Ninth Ground's Ten Dhāraṇīs of a Great Teacher (continued)

items.zh: 菩薩如是於諸有情六種攝受無倒轉時，當知遭遇略十二種艱難之事。聰叡菩薩於彼十二艱難之事當正覺了。何等十二？一者、於多安住違犯有情，若罰、若捨，是名菩薩遭艱難事。二者、於惡有情為調伏故，方便現行辛楚加行，防自意樂不生煩惱，是名菩薩遭艱難事。三者、現可施物極為尠少，現來求者其數彌多，是名菩薩遭艱難事。四者、唯有一身，眾多有情種種事業並現在前，同時來請共為助伴，是名菩薩遭艱難事。五者、居放逸處，若住世間可愛妙定，若生天上樂世界中，令心調善，是名菩薩遭艱難事。六者、常求遍作利有情事，而於此事無力無能，是名菩薩遭艱難事。七者、於其愚癡、諂詐、剛強諸有情所，若為說法、若復棄捨，是名菩薩遭艱難事。八者、常於生死見大過失，為度有情而不棄捨，是名菩薩遭艱難事。九者、未證清淨增上意樂，多分慮恐失念命終，是名菩薩遭艱難事。十者、未證清淨增上意樂，他來求乞第一最勝所可愛物，是名菩薩遭艱難事。十一者、種種異見、種種勝解諸有情類，若別教誨、若總棄捨，是名菩薩遭艱難事。十二者、常行最極不放逸行，而不應斷一切煩惱，是名菩薩遭艱難事。若諸菩薩遭遇如是諸艱難事，或於其中，應觀輕重，如其所應而作方便；或於其中，應審簡擇補特伽羅；或於其中，攀緣勇猛攝受因轉，若發正願；或於其中，制御其心，不令流散；或於其中，安住其心猛利思擇，不生厭倦而自安忍；或於其中，而行放捨；或於其中，發勤精進，熾然無懈；或於其中，善巧方便而正修行。菩薩如是於正對治方便善巧，雖遭一切諸艱難事正現在前，而無怯弱，自正能免。

blocks.text: Fascicle 48 ends with an honest list: twelve real dilemmas a bodhisattva faces in caring for beings, and how to meet them. **All of today's Chinese is untranslated.**

items: Among many who habitually do wrong: to discipline them, or to let them go.
Using harsh measures to tame wicked beings, while keeping one's own mind free of affliction.
Very little to give, and very many asking.
Only one body, and many beings asking for help with many tasks at the same time.
Living where heedlessness is easy (in pleasant worldly absorptions, or reborn in a happy heaven) and still keeping the mind well tamed.
Always wanting to benefit beings everywhere, yet lacking the power to do it.
Facing foolish, deceitful, stubborn beings: to teach them, or to leave them.
Seeing the great faults of saṃsāra, yet not abandoning it, in order to free beings.
Before attaining pure aspiration, fearing to die with mindfulness lost.
Before attaining pure aspiration, being asked for one's most precious possession.
Facing beings of many different views and convictions: to teach each separately, or to set them all aside.
Practising the utmost heedfulness, yet not cutting off every affliction (so as to remain in the world).

**How to meet them.** In some cases weigh what is heavier and lighter and act accordingly; in some, examine the particular person; in some, take courage and make a right vow; in some, rein in the mind so it does not scatter; in some, think hard and bear it without weariness; in some, let go; in some, strive with blazing diligence; in some, practise with skilful means. So, "though all these difficulties appear before them, they are not timid, and are able to come through".

blocks.text: From the second ground to the tenth, then births, care for beings, and these twelve dilemmas. The fascicle ends not with a vision of buddhahood but with practical problems: too little to give, too many asking, one body and many tasks. The treatise does not pretend the path is simple; it offers judgement rather than rules. Fascicle 49 continues the Bodhisattva Ground.

quiz.q: Which of these is one of the bodhisattva's twelve difficulties?
options: Having very little to give while very many are asking
Being born in a hell realm
quiz.why: "What can be given is very little, and those coming to ask are very many."

quiz.q: What does the treatise recommend for meeting these difficulties?
options: A single fixed rule for all cases
Different responses for different cases: weighing, examining the person, vowing, restraint, patience, letting go, diligence, skilful means
Asking a buddha in each case
quiz.why: The treatise gives a range of responses, chosen "as is fitting", rather than one rule.

quiz.q: Why is "practising the utmost heedfulness, yet not cutting off every affliction" a difficulty?
options: Because the bodhisattva keeps some affliction in order to remain in saṃsāra for beings, yet must not slip into heedlessness
Because it is a śrāvaka practice
quiz.why: This echoes Day 396: the bodhisattva keeps some seeds of affliction so as to go on taking birth for beings.
